title: Daylight Come And We Want Another Song; The Harder They Come Delivers With Both Song And Story

coordinate_points.label: Canon Theatre; Withrow Park
coordinate_points.production_title: The Harder They Come; The Menaechmus Twins

contact_edits.before: Another show with some songs (old-fashioned but nice) is The Menaechmus Twins, one of whose characters, a Roman slave, at one point makes as if about to sing about being free but then stops himself, as if he doesn't want to go into competition with Stephen Sondheim. This makes sense, as this play is by Plautus, whose ancient Roman comedies inspired A Funny Thing Happened on the Way to the Forum, though it's one that Forum didn't use. It did, though, inspire Shakespeare, whose Comedy of Errors added some sentiment and an extra pair of lookalikes. You may wonder if he really improved it much, since this open-air production is a total delight in its own right. Plautus at least explains why his long-separated twins should have the same first name, which is more than Shakespeare did. He also provided a tidier expository prologue, which the uncredited translation (in which someone "fills a fine freighter full of ... freight") gleefully exploits; as does Melee Hutton's production, brazenly presenting us with supposedly identical twins who are, at most, of about the same height. Wayne Ward gives a wonderfully self-satisfied account of the dark-haired married one, who finds himself excluded ( "I'm the most shuttest-out man alive") by wife and mistress, both of them played, as in some Freudian nightmare and deliciously, by the same actress, Sarah Evans. His fair-haired bachelor sibling is Ryan Hollyman, who plays on one flustered note but holds it well. Adrian Proszowski as one brother's servant and Jeffrey R. Smith as the other's parasite are towers of supporting strength. There is a basic two-door set, neatly used, and no need of lighting, since the show starts at 6 p. m. and is over at 7:20. It's early, short, hilarious and you pay what you can. The best theatrical deal in town. - The Harder They Come runs through Aug. 23 at the Canon Theatre. Call 416-872-1212 for ticket and schedule details. The Menaechmus Twins runs in Withrow Park through Aug. 9. Visit theatreworksproductions.comfor more information.
